sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Cliffside Park, NJ different?
sections.html:
Cliffside Park ranks fifth in population density among New Jersey's 565 municipalities, so a sale here may involve a condominium, a co-op unit or a house on a very small lot. The borough still requires a certificate of continued occupancy for a sale, issued through its building department, and the deed is filed in Hackensack through the Bergen County Clerk.

The borough covers less than one square mile, so distance to the bus lines on Anderson and Palisade Avenues and the view from the unit are easy points to describe in a listing. This page covers the local paperwork, the tax calendar and the Bergen County steps that apply when you sell.

sections.h2: Where is Cliffside Park and how did the borough form?
sections.html:
Cliffside Park sits on top of the Hudson Palisades in Bergen County, about 0.96 square miles in all, and it borders Edgewater, Fairview, Fort Lee and Ridgefield, with North Bergen in Hudson County to the south. The borough was created on January 15, 1895 from part of Ridgefield Township during the wave of borough formation that swept Bergen County in the 1890s, and its name describes the setting: a park by the cliffs.

Palisades Amusement Park, which straddled Cliffside Park and Fort Lee, ran from 1898 to 1971 on a 38-acre site, and high-rise apartment buildings now stand where the rides were. Gorge Road runs down the cliff face to the Edgewater waterfront, and the old place names Grantwood and Shadyside are still used for parts of the borough.

The middle owner-occupied value of $588,200 sits far above the national $332,700, and close to half the homes are not owner-occupied. A seller with a condo, a rented unit or an inherited multifamily building is dealing with a different market than a suburban house seller.

sections.h2: How do transit, roads and schools shape the Cliffside Park market?
sections.html:
Commute time is the headline number: the average trip to work runs 35.5 minutes, well above the 26.4 minutes for the country as a whole. Anderson Avenue and Palisade Avenue carry most north-south traffic, and Palisade Avenue has views toward the Hudson River and the Manhattan skyline. NJ Transit bus lines 156, 159 and 181 go to Manhattan, the 22 serves Jersey City, and the 751 and 755 run locally.

The Cliffside Park School District runs five schools, topped by Cliffside Park High School, which also takes students from Fairview under a sending and receiving arrangement. Students can apply to the Bergen County Technical Schools, including the academies in Hackensack. Because a large share of households speak a language other than English at home, about 65 percent by Census estimate, listing materials in more than one language can widen your buyer pool.

  • Name the bus line and the walking distance to it in your listing.
  • Photograph the view if you have one, and note which floor you are on.
  • For a condo or co-op, collect the association's budget and rules before the first showing.

sections.h2: What does the borough require before a Cliffside Park sale?
sections.html:
Cliffside Park's building department lists a Certificate of Occupancy as required for the sale of property. The department is at the Municipal Complex, 525 Palisade Avenue, Room 220, reachable at 201-313-2042, with counter hours of 8:30 to 4:30 The applications page carries a form titled Certificate of Continued Occupancy for Sale, with a separate form for rentals.

After the inspections are done and the requirements are met, the Construction Code Official issues either a Certificate of Occupancy or a Certificate of Approval. Work done on the property matters here: the department also issues permits for alterations, demolitions and interior renovations, so work done without a permit can surface during the sale. Cash is no longer taken in any borough department, so plan to pay by check, debit or credit card.

The Planning Board sits on the first Monday of each month and the Board of Adjustment on the fourth. Those dates matter if you need a variance before selling. The current charge for the sale certificate is on the borough's own form, so ask the department before you file.

sections.h2: How and when are Cliffside Park property taxes paid?
sections.html:
Cliffside Park collects real estate tax in four installments, on the first of February, May, August and November. The tax collector sits on the second floor of 525 Palisade Avenue, and the phone is 201-313-2050. You can pay through the borough's online lookup page, mail a check to the Tax Collector at that address, or use the drop box by the Borough Hall entrance.

The borough has published figures showing a modest bill by Bergen County standards. A borough release reported an average residence assessed at $373,110 with an annual bill of $9,982, the ninth lowest among the county's 70 municipalities, based on state Department of Community Affairs data. That release reflects an earlier tax year, so use your own current bill for closing math.

For state relief programs, the finance page points to the Division of Taxation's relief page. If you receive a homestead benefit and sell, the state's selling guide says to mark the move on the application or take the benefit as a credit at closing, otherwise it is applied to the new owner's taxes.

sections.h2: Can you appeal a Cliffside Park assessment before selling?
sections.html:
You can, through the Bergen County Board of Taxation in Hackensack, but timing is strict. The state filing date is April 1, moved to May 1 after a revaluation, and the Bergen board's own page says the 2026 deadline has gone by. The board encourages online filing and can be reached at 201-336-6300. Start with the borough assessor at 201-313-2009, whose office also defends appeals.

The board's guidance is blunt: your current assessment is assumed correct, and you must show it is unreasonable compared with market value. Evidence means recent comparable sales, not a complaint about the tax bill. An appeal mainly benefits whoever owns the property after the ruling, so ask your attorney whether filing makes sense before a sale.

  • Compare your assessment with recent sales of similar units in your building or block.
  • Check that the assessor shows the correct square footage and unit count.
  • Ask whether a pending appeal could affect the closing adjustments.

sections.h2: What happens to the deed and the state fees on a higher-priced Cliffside Park sale?
sections.html:
The Bergen County Clerk handles the filing and keeps the county's deeds, mortgages and liens. The seller owes the state realty transfer fee, and above $1,000,000 a graduated percent fee applies on residential and cooperative-unit deeds: 1 percent of the total price between $1,000,000 and $2,000,000, rising to 3.5 percent above $3,500,000. With a middle value of $588,200, most Cliffside Park sales land under that line, but a penthouse or a multifamily building can cross it. In addition, the buyer pays a separate 1 percent fee on certain purchases above $1 million.

Every seller also gives a gross income tax form at closing. A New Jersey resident signs a residency certification. An owner who has left New Jersey prepays estimated income tax, calculated at either two percent of the price or the 8.97 percent rate on the gain. Separately, the federal rule for a principal residence can shelter $250,000 of profit, or $500,000 for a married couple.

sections.h2: Which routes sell a Cliffside Park home fastest?
sections.html:
Two routes move fastest: an investor purchase, or a well-priced listing with the certificate already in hand. A unit with a clean inspection history and complete association paperwork leaves a buyer fewer open questions.

If you inherited a unit, have tenants or owe back taxes, get permit status and a tax payoff in writing before you accept an offer. An as-is buyer will still need the occupancy certificate and a clear deed, so those items belong on your checklist whichever route you choose.

faqs.q: Is a certificate required to sell in Cliffside Park?
faqs.a: Yes. The borough building department lists a Certificate of Occupancy as required for the sale of property, and its applications page carries a separate sale form.

faqs.q: Where is the Cliffside Park sale certificate filed?
faqs.a: At the building department, Municipal Complex, 525 Palisade Avenue, Room 220, or by phone at 201-313-2042. The borough accepts check, debit or credit card, not cash.

faqs.q: What are the Cliffside Park tax installment dates?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November. You can pay online, by mail, or in the drop box by the Borough Hall entrance.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Cliffside Park assessment for 2026?
faqs.a: No. The Bergen County Board of Taxation says the 2026 filing deadline has gone by. Later appeals are due April 1, or May 1 after a revaluation.

faqs.q: Which office records a Cliffside Park deed?
faqs.a: The Bergen County Clerk in Hackensack files deeds and mortgages for the borough, usually through your attorney or title agent along with the state fee and income tax forms.
